title: Priority P0: Investigate and mitigate cross-environment TTFT degradation affecting multi-region routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Starting 2025-02-10 23:40 UTC, we received multiple customer escalations reporting increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) and lower tokens/sec for the redwood-v1-large family across Hosted and Dedicated deployments in EU and us-west. Initial alerts showed a ~2-4x TTFT increase on median P50 for streaming requests and sustained throttle on per-tenant TPS. Investigation discovered an interaction between the new scheduler reorder heuristic (merged in runtime-1.20) and the multi-region routing path that caused delayed KV cache warms and elevated queueing for cross-region fallbacks.

Impact: High — revenue impact for 5 enterprise customers using Dedicated pools and multiple Hosted customers. Symptoms included long single-token latencies (~800ms -> 2s) for many short prompts and a drop in overall tokens/sec for inference pipelines. Observed across models using the new attention kernel selection path but most visible for redwood-v1-large and its quantized variants.

Root cause hypothesis: The scheduler heuristic (prefers local batching to maximize GPU utilization) introduced longer per-request requeue windows when routing policy triggered a fallback (region/variant). When a request hit a fallback path, the runtime attempted a sync transfer of KV state and a tokenization-buffer flush. Under bursty traffic the heuristic pushed fallback requests behind larger batches, causing cold-KV penalties and token emission delay. Additionally, a regression in the per-tenant token-rate limiter miscalculated active window size when requests spanned shards, effectively applying a conservative throttle.

Work done so far: 1) Reproduced locally with synthetic traces and captured kernel-level traces for affected requests. 2) Added debug logs around scheduler batch decision and KV transfer for two customers' request traces. 3) Scoped the regression to commit 3f6b7a (scheduler reorder) and a follow-up change 4a9c1e (rate limiter tweak). 4) Implemented a short-term mitigation: a runtime flag to disable reorder heuristic for cross-region fallbacks and a guard to bypass conservative rate-limiter when KV warming is detected. 5) Deployed emergency canary (runtime-1.20.1-canary) to a subset of hosted traffic and one Dedicated customer; early signals show TTFT returning to baseline within 15 minutes of flip.

Proposed fix: Ship runtime-1.20.1 with the following changes: a) revert the reorder heuristic for requests that are routed to fallback variants or regions; b) add a KV-warmup async path that warms remote caches without blocking first-token emission; c) correct rate-limiter window calculation to use shard-coordinated counters. Follow-up: design a non-regressive scheduler heuristic in runtime-1.21 that accounts for cross-region fallback latency and prioritizes first-token emission for low-latency SLAs.

Rollback plan: If rollout shows regressions, flip the safety flag to re-enable previous behavior globally (already exercised in canary). If instability persists, revert runtime to 1.19-based patch build for affected pools.

Next steps: a) Complete PR review and merge for runtime-1.20.1 patch. b) Coordinate with SRE to run a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). c) Notify affected customers with timeline and mitigations. d) Add an eval to the Optimize pipeline to detect similar regressions for future merges.
